title.narrative: Support to the Solomon Islands to reduce the incidence of Malaria and Tuberculosis - Solomon Islands (01-Jan-2024-31-Dec-2026)

description.narrative: Solomon Islands, Multicomponent, World Vision International (WV Solomon Islands)This program has the following goals: Reduce national API from a targeted rate of 155/1000 in 2024 to 89/1000 in by 2026.. Zero malaria deaths by 2026. TB incidence reduced by 15% by 2026 from 65 per 100,000 population in 2021. Strengthen the Solomon Islands National TB Program and build resilient systems to improve access to quality TB care by 2026. The objectives of this program are: To maintain high LLIN coverage, increase usage to bring down malaria cases. To maximise access to and utilisation of early laboratory-confirmed diagnosis and appropriate treatment for malaria.. Improve surveillance in low burden settings for targeted elimination interventions. To support the Ministry of Health in evidence based decision making by strengthening TB Surveillance and Reporting. To support the TB program to accelerate progress towards TB Elimination by strengthening Diagnosis and Case Finding. To reduce TB Catastrophic costs by improving access to TB Treatment and Community-based TB Care. To reduce TB Transmission by strengthening Infection prevention control

title.narrative: Coverage / Output indicators targets and results for SLB-Z-WVIP01
Percentage of districts that produce at least semi-annual analytical reports
Timeliness of reporting: Percentage of submitted monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are received on time per the national guidelines
Percentage of new and relapse TB patients tested using WHO recommended rapid diagnostic tests at the time of diagnosis
Completeness of reporting: Percentage of expected monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are actually received

Treatment success rate- all forms: Percentage of patients with all forms of TB, bacteriologically confirmed plus clinically diagnosed, successfully treated (cured plus treatment completed) among all TB patients notified during a specified period; *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Proportion of suspected malaria cases that receive a parasitological test at public sector health facilities
Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment at public sector health facilities
Number of patients with of all forms of TB notified (i.e., bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed); *includes only those with new and relapse TB
Number of people in contact with TB patients who began preventive therapy
Number of insecticide-treated nets distributed to populations at risk of malaria transmission through mass campaigns
Number of insecticide-treated nets distributed to targeted risk groups through continuous distribution
